nodes.name: Plasma pretreatment of carbon cloth
nodes.procedure: The carbon cloth was cut into 1 × 2 cm pieces and ultrasonically cleaned with ethanol and deionized water for 20 min before use, then dried. The prepared carbon cloth was placed inside a plasma vacuum chamber, where the vacuum was drawn down to 3 Pa. Nitrogen (N2) and argon (Ar) gases were then introduced at flow rates of 40 and 80 sccm, respectively. The microwave plasma was set to 300 W and the treatment was carried out for 15 min, resulting in plasma-pretreated carbon cloth, named pCC.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Co(OH)2
nodes.procedure: To prepare the electrolyte for electrodeposition, 1.455 g of Co(NO3)2·6H2O was measured and dissolved in 100 mL of deionized water, followed by ultrasonic dispersion for 20 min and magnetic stirring for 1 h. Electrochemical deposition was conducted using a three-electrode system... The electrodeposition was performed in constant voltage mode, setting the voltage to -1.1 V vs Ag/AgCl, for a deposition duration of 15 min. After deposition, the working electrode surface was rinsed with deionized water and air-dried at 60°C overnight to obtain the catalyst precursor on a self-supporting electrode.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images of p-Co3O4 show vertical flake-featured morphology similar to a-Co3O4 with negligible impact from plasma treatment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The similar SEM images of p-Co3O4 to a-Co3O4 indicate that the different post-treatments have a negligible impact on the sample morphology (Figure 3c,d).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM image of p-Co3O4 manifests numerous fine crystalline nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image of p-Co3O4 given in Figure 3e manifests numerous fine crystalline nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern of p-Co3O4 demonstrates characteristic polycrystalline diffraction ring aligning with standard spinel Co3O4 structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern depicted in Figure 3f demonstrates a characteristic polycrystalline diffraction ring that aligns with the standard diffraction pattern for the spinel structure Co3O4.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM image of p-Co3O4 shows irregularity of crystal plane arrangement with abundant defects and crystal plane staggering.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of p-Co3O4 shows the irregularity of the crystal plane arrangement, exiting abundant defects and crystal plane staggering (Figure 3g).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Co and O species on p-Co3O4 surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping given in Figure 3h shows a uniform distribution of Co and O species on the p-Co3O4 surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of p-Co3O4 and a-Co3O4 show Co3O4 phase (JCPDS #74-2120) with broader diffraction peaks for p-Co3O4 (crystallite size 40 Å) vs a-Co3O4 (100 Å).
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the XRD patterns of p-Co3O4 and a-Co3O4, the peaks of α-Co(OH)2 completely disappear and are replaced by the diffraction peak of Co3O4 (JCPDS #74-2120) (Figure 4a). Notably, the diffraction peaks of p-Co3O4 are broader than those of a-Co3O4, and crystallite size calculations based on the peak half-width are 40 Å for p-Co3O4 and 100 Å for a-Co3O4, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra of p-Co3O4 show red shift compared to a-Co3O4, attributed to reduced crystallite dimensions and presence of defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Simultaneously, the Raman spectra reveal a red shift in the signals of p-Co3O4 compared with those of a-Co3O4, which is attributed to the reduced crystallite dimensions as well as the presence of defects (Figure 4b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p XPS shows Co²⁺ peak at 781.5 eV with increased intensity for p-Co3O4 (indicating Co³⁺→Co²⁺ conversion by O defects) vs a-Co3O4 (Co³⁺ 780.0 eV, Co²⁺ 781.7 eV); O 1s shows peaks at 530.1 eV (Co-O), 531.4 eV (Ov), 532.5 eV (adsorbed H2O) with higher Ov intensity in p-Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For a-Co3O4 the peaks at 780.0 and 781.7 eV correspond to Co³⁺ and Co²⁺ respectively... In contrast, the Co²⁺ peak for p-Co3O4 is shifted to 781.5 eV accompanied by increased intensity, indicating that the introduction of O defects alters the electronic structure of Co, converting Co³⁺ to Co²⁺. The O 1s XPS spectrum of the two samples show peaks at 530.1, 531.4, and 532.5 eV, corresponding to Co-O, Ov, and adsorbed water molecules, respectively... The increased intensity of the ionization of the Ov signal in p-Co3O4 suggests a higher defect concentration (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR results corroborate presence of more oxygen vacancies in p-Co3O4 than a-Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EPR results given in Figure 4e further corroborate the presence of more Ov in p-Co3O4.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES indicates lower Co oxidation state in p-Co3O4 vs standard Co3O4; FT-EXAFS fitting shows significantly lower O coordination number in p-Co3O4 (Table S2); WT-EXAFS shows increased K position of Co-O bond in p-Co3O4 due to electron redistribution from O defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co K-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure shown in Figure 4f indicates a lower oxidation state of Co in p-Co3O4 compared to standard Co3O4. The fitting results of Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) in R and k spaces confirm that the number of coordinations of the O in p-Co3O4 is significantly lower than that in standard Co3O4 (Figures 4g and S12 and Table S2). The wavelet transform of EXAFS (WT-EXAFS) analysis on Co K-edge shows that the K position of the Co-O bond in p-Co3O4 is increased, attributed to the redistribution of electrons around the atoms caused by O defects (Figure 4h and i).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman of p-Co3O4 in 0.1 M HClO4 shows O-O coupling peak at 1050 cm⁻¹ appearing at 1.75 V, confirming DOM pathway.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For a-Co3O4 as the voltage increases, the signal peak corresponding to the O-O coupling peak at 1050 cm⁻¹ is not observed, while for p-Co3O4 it appears at 1.75 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faradaic region at various scan rates gives Cdl values yielding ECSA of 31.7 cm² for p-Co3O4 and 24.1 cm² for a-Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further, by recording the cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves in the nonFaradaic region at various scan rates (Figure S14), the double-layer capacitance (Cdl) of the samples was obtained to determine the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA)... The results reveal that Co(OH)2 has the lowest ECSA, while the ECSA values of a-Co3O4 and p-Co3O4 are 24.1 cm² and 31.7 cm², respectively (Figure S15a).
